summary: The note follows James Carter, owner of the 'Bean There, Sipped That' café, as he builds a digital presence over roughly a year from October 2023, with help from consultant Vanessa Richardson and analyst Cynthia Lee. It walks through the steps he took: a website and SEO, social media, analytics, email marketing, paid ads and online reputation management. It closes by noting the ongoing challenges and the need for adaptability among small businesses.
one_line: Café owner James Carter's step-by-step digital marketing journey illustrates how small businesses can build online presence through SEO, social media, analytics, email, ads and reputation management.
key_facts: James Carter owns the café 'Bean There, Sipped That' and noticed declining regular customer footfall in October 2023, prompting his digital turn.
Industry studies cited in the note said 97% of consumers turned to the web to find local services and products.
Carter launched a new website on November 1, 2023, and by early December improved his Google search rankings through keywords and a coffee culture blog.
Vanessa Richardson, a digital marketing consultant, was enlisted by Carter on December 22 and urged him to use Instagram and Facebook.
A January 2024 survey cited by Richardson found over 50% of small business revenue was generated through social connections.
Cynthia Lee, a data analyst recruited in March, showed that the 'Espresso Mondays' campaign drove more business than any signage Carter had displayed in the past year.
By late March 2024, Lee built a dashboard showing peak engagement times, customer demographics and the content types that resonated most.
Carter launched an email newsletter in April 2024, and a 'bring-a-friend' coupon produced a record number of lattes served on a sunny day in late April.
In May, Carter began paid online advertising with a modest budget and, after weeks of trial and error, succeeded with localized ads pitching the café as the neighborhood nook.
Lee said 'In targeting, specificity is key', and June data showed a higher click-through rate for ads aimed at the local community and lifestyle.
In July a string of negative online comments threatened Carter's brand; Richardson coached him to respond promptly and empathetically, turning critics into loyal advocates by August.
The note states that as of October 10, 2023, the struggle for small business online visibility had never been more intense.
